definition: Polars is a very fast DataFrame library written in Rust, with a lazy query engine that runs on all CPU cores.
details: Created by Ritchie Vink in 2020; developed by the open-source community and the company Polars Inc.

explainer.lead: How to install Polars, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Created by Ritchie Vink; backed by Polars Inc.

quickstart.python:
import polars as pl

df = pl.read_csv("events.csv")
out = (
    df.lazy()
      .filter(pl.col("score") > 0.5)
      .group_by("label")
      .agg(pl.len().alias("n"), pl.col("score").mean())
      .collect()
)
print(out)

explainer.inAi: Swap it in for pandas when feature engineering on millions of rows gets slow; the lazy API lets Polars plan and parallelise the whole pipeline.

tiers.eli5: It's like a spreadsheet program built to split the work across every worker at once instead of one row at a time.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use its lazy engine to build and optimize query plans before execution on big tables. A pitfall is expecting pandas-compatible behavior, since APIs and some semantics differ.
tiers.paperLevel: Data operations are expressed as a lazy query plan that the engine optimizes before execution, parallelized across available CPU cores. Performance depends on available cores and memory rather than a single-threaded path.

explainer.example: A lazy pipeline filters and aggregates a multi-gigabyte table, with the engine executing the plan in parallel across all cores.
